Mathematics Ph.D. Program Requirements
Overview
The Ph.D. program in Mathematics at UC Irvine is designed to train students in advanced mathematics and prepare them for research and professional careers. The program involves a progression through foundational coursework, qualifying and comprehensive examinations, coursework in a major area of specialization, advancement to candidacy, teaching experience, and completion and defense of an original dissertation. Below is a concise summary of the main requirements for completion of the Ph.D. in Mathematics at UC Irvine.
DocuSign Form Submission Process ⚠️
Step 1 — Click on the appropriate DocuSign form link and fill in the required recipient fields as follows:
Dept Form Preparer — Your name and email
Committee Members — Names and emails of all committee members
Chair of Doctoral Committee — Your advisor’s name and email
Student — Your name and email
Department Chair/Grad Advisor — Name: “Knut Solna” | Email: ksolna@uci.edu
Associate Dean — Leave blank
Department Copy — Name: “Dept of Math” | Email: mathgrad@uci.edu
⚠️ Double-check all email addresses before submitting. Incorrect emails will cause delays.
Step 2 — Click “Begin Signing” and fill out your portion of the form (name, student ID, school/department, committee members), then click “Finish.” The form will automatically route to your committee members for their signatures.
Step 3 —Once all committee members have signed, the form will return to you for any remaining student signatures. DocuSign will indicate where to sign.
Step 4 — The form will then route to Vice Chair Solna for his signature.
Step 5 — After all signatures are collected, the form is automatically sent to the Graduate Division. No action needed on your part.
Requirements Summary
Core Coursework
Incoming students are expected to complete the following sequences by the end of their second year, with a grade of B or better:
Math 210 ABC (Real Analysis)
Math 220 ABC (Complex Analysis)
Math 230 ABC (Algebra)
(Some students may need to take Math 205 as preparation based on assessment at end of Jumpstart and placement exam.)
1st and 2nd years: Enroll in Math 298ABC Graduate Seminar for Fall, Winter and Spring quarters.
Only one of the courses Mathematics 210A-B-C, 220A-B-C, and 230A-B-C may count for the course requirement.
All course requirements must be satisfied before advancement.
Qualifying and Comprehensive Exams
By the start of the second year: Achieve at least two passes at the M.S. level among the respective qualification exams in Analysis Comprehensive (205), Real Analysis (210), Complex Analysis (220), Algebra (230), or Applied Mathematics (290).
By the start of the third year: Achieve at least two passes at the Ph.D. level among the four areas (210, 220, 230, 290).
All Exams are offered in June and in September. The schedule for these exams will be made available on our website (insert web link here).
Maximum three attempts for each exam, however the exams after Jumpstart in September before your first year do not count towards the maximum number of attempts.
Passing a Qualifying Exam at the Ph.D. level exempts the student from that corresponding sequence (example: if you pass the Algebra (230) Qualifying Exam you are exempt from taking the Math 230 sequence).
Specialization/Course Requirements and Advisor Selection
By the end of the second year, students must declare a major specialization in one of:
Algebra
Analysis
Applied & Computational Mathematics
Geometry & Topology
Logic
Probability
Students must complete two series of courses (ABC) in their chosen specialty and two series outside (ABC) their specialization. Special topics courses (excluding Math 205) may count (Please consult with Advisor/Vice-Chair/Student Affairs Officer for course eligibility).
Please refer to Course Specialization Overview for which courses count for each specialization.
Students must also enroll in the Math Grad Seminar course (Math 298ABC) for the first 2 years.
By the beginning of the third year, students select an advisor specializing in their major area.

Advisor and Committee Selection
Form an advancement committee of five senate (tenure) faculty members, including at least one (but no more than two) members (also tenured faculty) from outside the department.
Please submit the “Approval of Advancement Committee” form to the department to verify each faculty member is eligible to be on your committee. You can find the form below
The form needs to be completed at least 3 weeks prior to your scheduled advancement.
Approval of Advancement Committee Form
Advancement to Candidacy
By the beginning of the fourth year, students must:
Have satisfied all coursework and exam requirements
Submit a document which gives the foundation for the advancement presentation to the advancement committee at least 3 days prior to advancement exam.
Pass an oral Advancement to Candidacy examination.
After passing exam complete Ph. D. Advancement to Candidacy Form (Ph.D. form I)
Advancement Policy & Filing Deadlines
Ph. D. Advancement To Candidacy Form (Ph. D. form I)
Dissertation
Following advancement to candidacy, students undertake independent, original research in their area of specialization, culminating in a written dissertation. The dissertation must be publicly defended before a thesis committee (a subcommittee of the advancement committee, at least three faculty (can be one outside member), chaired by the advisor. Students must:
Submit a version of the dissertation to the thesis committee at least 3 days prior to the defense.
After dissertation defense fill out Ph. D. Doctoral Dissertation Checklist & Final Degree Paperwork (Ph. D. form II)

Additional Notes
Financial support is typically provided for up to 6 years (Maximum time permitted in program: 7 years (7th year is not financially supported).
The Ph.D. must be completed within 9 quarters (three years) after advancement to candidacy.
Only one of the core sequences (Math 210ABC, 220ABC, 230ABC) can count towards the advancement coursework requirement.
Students may not use a Ph. D pass of a qualifying exam to satisfy both coursework and exam requirements.
Example: If you use 230 exam to satisfy the Ph. D qualification requirement then you cannot use the 230 sequence to satisfy the requirement related to taking 2 series inside and 2 series outside of a specialization.
However, you are exempt from the requirement of taking 230 as a core sequence.
Even if you have more than two Ph. D passes you cannot use the qualification exam passes to satisfy course requirements related to taking 2 series inside and 2 series outside of a specialization.
The core sequences (210,220 and 230) cannot be used to satisfy course requirements if the student uses that corresponding sequence area to satisfy the Ph. D qualification exam requirement.
Example: You cannot use the completed 230ABC sequence to satisfy the 230 Qualification exam if you’re using the completed 230ABC sequence to satisfy your course requirements.
Ph. D Requirements Summarized
Completion of the PhD: Average completion time is 5.8 years; maximum time permitted is seven years. The Department will not
financially support students past their sixth year in the PhD program. Completion of the PhD degree must occur within 9 quarters (three years) of advancement to PhD candidacy. Passing grade for coursework is a B or better.
